messages:
pagerduty-bot: ALERT: High p50/p95 latency on redwood-runtime-prod (kv-cache miss rate spike) · Pager #4387 · https://pagerduty.example/alerts/4387

sre-oncall: seeing a spike in continuous-batcher queue times, starts ~09:12 UTC. p95 > 2s on text-gen endpoints. Lots of toolcall-invoke traces.

ingrid-engineer: yup traffic correlation shows recent surge in requests with structured function outputs — many unique tool call signatures, different schemas. KV cache key count jumped 18x.

sre-oncall: assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml. tagging @ben-runtime @alice-ml. I'm paging customers impacted.

ben-runtime: on it. initial hypothesis: structured tool outputs cause variable prefixing in prompt/ctx which defeats prefix/KV caching and fragments continuous batches. cache working set suddenly huge -> eviction churn -> latency.

alice-ml: confirm. I see many toolcall chains returning slightly different JSON keys and nested arrays — our cache keys include normalized prompt+schema which isn't normalizing variants. Means less reuse.

sre-oncall: how bad is customer impact? product-ops, cs? @customer-success any calls?

customer-success: CS queue has 3 customers reporting timeouts/higher latency for inference calls, two on dedicated pools. One mentioned errors when toolcalls returned nested arrays briefly. They're escalated.

product-ops: marking incident sev=2 for now. Need mitigation ASAP. Can we throttle structured-toolcall prefetch or disable continuous batching for affected models?

ben-runtime: we can flip a rollout flag to force batch_mode=static for model-family xlarge-mix, or set max_batch_size=8 and batch_timeout=20ms. Quick toggle via infra CLI.

sre-oncall: do it. post the exact command here so deploy-bot can run.

ben-runtime: running in a sec. command:```rbctl set cluster redwood-prod runtime.batch_config --model-family xlarge-mix --max_batch_size 8 --batch_window_ms 20 --disable_continuous_batching true```

deploy-bot: @ben-runtime executing command on redwood-prod. Starting rollout to 6/12 pools. ETA ~ 90s.

deploy-bot: rollout step 1 complete (6 pools). Observability: p95 latency down 30% in those pools.

ingrid-engineer: seeing immediate reduction in KV key churn where rollout applied, cache miss ratio drops. overall miss-rate still elevated due to remaining pools.

deploy-bot: rollout completed to all pools. Full apply done at 09:18:43 UTC.

sre-oncall: metrics look better. p95 back to baseline for most endpoints, still minor blips on dedicated nodes.

alice-ml: short-term mitigation looks good. Need to follow up: fix cache key normalization for toolcall structured outputs — strip variable array indices & normalize schema keys ordering.

ben-runtime: agreed. Also propose adding a heuristic to limit new cache entries per minute per model to avoid runaway cache growth on schema churn.

product-ops: CS, please draft customer-facing note: impacted calls, mitigation applied, ETA for root cause fix.

customer-success: will draft and send to the three customers within 1h.

sre-oncall: logging timeline: alert 09:12, mitigation rollout start 09:16, full apply 09:18:43, p95 recovery 09:20. Root cause: structured toolcall variants caused cache fragmentation -> eviction churn -> latency.

ben-runtime: quick postmortem action items: (1) revert single-flip if rollback needed (we can), (2) short-term patch to normalize schema keys in cache key, (3) implement per-model cache-entry-rate limiter, (4) add metric alert for sudden cache-key-cardinality growth.

alice-ml: dev task: add test cases for toolcall permutations to our eval harness so we catch regression in CI.

ingrid-engineer: will create infra PR for key-normalization + instrumentation. ETA for dev/qa: 2 working days, staging validation 1 day.

product-ops: scheduling follow-up incident review 48h. Add SLO impact numbers and customer list.

sre-oncall: closing active pager. If anything regresses reopen. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: NOTE: change was non-disruptive, no restarts. Audit id: rb-audit-2026-05-13-09-18-43

sre-oncall: saving this thread as incident record. We'll include logs and traces in the postmortem doc.
